facts: Deed from Thomas Wend to his son Aaron Wend, residential parcel, gift. Aaron lives in the home year round but lists a spare bedroom on a short-term rental site, renting it for a total of 9 days during the calendar year. No other business use. The parcel is classified as residential real property under MCL 211.34c. The deed was recorded in March 2026.

expected.notes: TRAP — subsection precision. 27a(11)(c) defines 'commercial purpose' to EXCLUDE rental of residential real property for fewer than 15 days in a calendar year. 9 days does not defeat the (u) exception. A model that sees 'rental' and reflexively uncaps fails this. [FACTS TIGHTENED 2026-08-04, systematic audit: the statute defines 'residential real property' as property CLASSIFIED as such under section 34c, and the family/trust exceptions in (7)(u), (7)(g)(ii) and (7)(v) all begin 'Beginning December 31, 2014'. Cases that said only 'residential parcel' with no date left the model unable to tell (7)(t) from (7)(u) — which is what made TD-FAMRES-003 fail before it was fixed the same way. Classification and a transfer date are now stated wherever they are load-bearing. The legal question each case tests is unchanged.]
